Evaluate improvement in staff awareness and preparedness to confirm effectiveness
Outsource them to the NCSC
Repeat the same course every month
quiz.explanation: OM-5.5.54 requires the bank to evaluate improvement in the level of awareness and preparedness to deal with cyber risk, to make sure the training is effective.

quiz.question: Which examples of certifications does OM-5.5.11(d) give for cyber security staff training?
options: CFA, ACCA and FRM
Security+, CEH, CISSP, CISA and CISM
PMP, PRINCE2 and ITIL
CAMS, CGSS and CFE
quiz.explanation: OM-5.5.11(d) says senior management must provide and require regular cyber security update and training sessions for cyber staff, with examples such as Security+, CEH, CISSP, CISA and CISM.

quiz.question: Under OM-5.5.50, which stakeholders should the bank's programme of incident response exercises take into account?
options: Only external penetration testers
Only the IT help desk
Technical staff, the crisis management team, decision-makers and spokespersons
Only customers and the media
quiz.explanation: OM-5.5.50 asks for an exercise programme using simulations, war games and table-tops, with reference to technical staff, the crisis team, decision-makers and spokespersons.

quiz.question: What is a recovery point objective (RPO) in Module OM?
options: The time by which a service must be back
The date of the next penetration test
The maximum fine for a late report
The point to which data must be restored for the activity to work again
quiz.explanation: OM-5.5.47 defines RTO as the time in which a process must be recovered and RPO as the point to which information must be restored so the activity can operate on resumption.

quiz.question: Before returning a recovered system to normal operation after a cyber incident, what does OM-5.5.49 say the bank should check?
options: That it is free of compromise, fully working, secure and its data intact
Only that customers can log in
That the insurer has paid the claim
That the CBB has visited the site
quiz.explanation: OM-5.5.49 says recovered assets should be validated as free of compromise, fully functional and meeting security requirements, including data integrity checks.

quiz.question: How does OM-5.5.53 describe the way a bank should approach cyber risk insurance?
options: Insurance is optional and discouraged
Buy the cheapest policy without assessment
The CBB provides the insurance directly
Seek cover after a cyber risk assessment that the insurer independently verifies
quiz.explanation: OM-5.5.53 requires banks to arrange to seek cyber risk insurance from a suitable insurer after a risk-based assessment that the insurer independently verifies.

quiz.question: What did the CBB's August 2026 event with the National Cyber Security Center focus on?
options: Securing financial services data in the AI era, including the human element
New capital requirements for banks
Licensing rules for exchange houses
Changes to Bahrain's currency notes
quiz.explanation: The CBB said the event, 'Securing Financial Services Data in the AI Era', covered the human element in cyber security and AI-related trends, to raise readiness across all roles and job levels.

regulators: National Cybersecurity Center, Ministry of Interior (NCSC)

references.title: Operational Risk Management Module (Module OM), Volume 1: copy issued with the January 2024 consultation on cyber security amendments
references.provision: Section OM-5.5 (OM-5.5.1 to OM-5.5.61), including training OM-5.5.54-5.5.56 and reporting OM-5.5.57-5.5.58
references.note: CBB-hosted copy published with the 28 January 2024 consultation. Pages dated July 2021, April 2022 and October 2022 show the rules then in force; pages marked 'XX 2024' show proposals (for example threat intelligence and attack surface management).

references.title: Central Bank of Bahrain and Financial Institutions Law (Law No. 64 of 2006)
references.note: Customer information is confidential and a licensee may disclose it only with the customer's unequivocal approval, under law or treaty, by court order or on CBB instruction; recipients are bound too, and bad-faith disclosure is an offence.

references.title: Financial Cybersecurity Controls (National Cybersecurity Center draft v0.1, issued by the CBB for consultation)
references.issuer: Ministry of Interior, National Cybersecurity Center / Central Bank of Bahrain
references.note: Draft national standard consulted on in November 2022; would require an approved awareness programme, role-based training and an annual effectiveness review. Mentioned only as a consultation; final status not confirmed.

references.title: Law No. (30) of 2018 with respect to Personal Data Protection
references.issuer: Kingdom of Bahrain (Legislation and Legal Opinion Commission)
references.note: General data protection law supervised by the Personal Data Protection Authority. The official text could not be opened, so the quest covers it only in general terms.

references.title: CBB consultations page (cyber security consultations 2020, 2022 and 28 January 2024)
references.note: Lists the January 2020 cyber security risk management consultation, the June 2022 cybersecurity requirements consultation, the November 2022 Financial Cybersecurity Controls consultation and the 28 January 2024 proposed amendments.

references.title: Warning- Benefitpay SMS
references.note: January 2021 public warning about a fake SMS claiming the user's Benefitpay CPR number had expired, with a shortened link; Benefitpay never requests personal information by SMS.

references.title: CBB warns consumers when dealing with personal and banking information
references.note: September 2020 warning, prompted by a global rise in cyber attacks and fraud during COVID-19, on fake calls, messages and websites seeking banking information.

references.title: CBB warns against fraudulent scam involving the impersonation of Cyprus Securities and Exchange Commission
references.note: June 2019 warning describing genuine-looking emails with copied regulator logos and signatures used to seek fees and personal information.

references.title: CBB organizes Specialized Cyber Security Awareness Event in coordination with NCSC
references.note: August 2026 awareness event for financial sector professionals, 'Securing Financial Services Data in the AI Era', on the human element and AI trends.

references.title: Bahrain's Banking and Financial Sector Continues to Operate Normally, Demonstrating Stability, Resilience and the Highest Levels of Readiness
references.note: March 2026 statement: heightened CBB oversight during regional developments, continuity across institutions, and physical and cyber security measures at the highest readiness.

bank.question: Dilmun Coast Bank's board approved the cyber framework two years ago. The CBB examiner asks for evidence that cyber security is discussed at board level. Which evidence best meets OM-5.5.1 and OM-5.5.4?
options: The approval letter from two years ago
The IT department's monthly ticket statistics
Board minutes showing cyber as an agenda item, with reports on indicators, maturity, awareness, incidents and test results
A contract with the bank's antivirus vendor
bank.explanation: OM-5.5.1 makes cyber security an item for discussion at board or board committee meetings, and OM-5.5.4 expects comprehensive reports at every meeting covering those topics. A one-off approval does not show ongoing oversight.

bank.question: The cyber risk function at a Bahraini conventional bank reports to the CIO, who also runs IT operations. Which change brings it into line with OM-5.5.6?
options: Rename it the IT security unit
Move its reporting line to an independent risk management function
Ask internal audit to review it every five years
Let the CIO approve its reports before they reach the board
bank.explanation: OM-5.5.6 requires a cyber security risk function independent of the IT department that reports to an independent risk management function or equivalent. Renaming or audit reviews do not fix the reporting line.

bank.question: Which combination of review cycles is correct under Module OM-5.5?
options: Policy every three years; strategy annually; framework only on CBB request
Policy and strategy every five years; framework annually
Policy quarterly; strategy every two years; framework every five years
Policy at least annually; strategy at least every three years; framework every three years or on significant change
bank.explanation: OM-5.5.15 sets an annual review of the policy, OM-5.5.14 a revision of the strategy at least every three years, and OM-5.5.5 an evaluation of the framework every three years or on significant change.

bank.question: Thomas, the CRO, is asked to chair the bank's cyber security committee. Which membership is closest to what OM-5.5.9 suggests?
options: Only IT engineers and the external auditor
Board members and shareholders only
Customer representatives and vendors
Senior managers from business functions, IT, risk and compliance
bank.explanation: OM-5.5.9 says the committee should be headed by an independent senior manager from a control function and include senior managers from business functions, IT, risk and compliance.

bank.question: Dilmun Coast Bank is drafting its cyber strategy. Which element does OM-5.5.13 require the scope of risk identification and assessment to include?
options: The personal social media of staff
Dependencies on third-party service providers
Competitors' marketing plans
Exchange rate forecasts
bank.explanation: OM-5.5.13(e) requires the strategy's scope of risk identification and assessment to include dependencies on third-party service providers.

bank.question: The bank's cyber policy lists access, incident and vulnerability management but not cyber training and awareness. What is the problem under OM-5.5.15?
options: Cyber training and awareness is one of the policy areas that must be addressed
None, since training belongs only in the HR manual
The policy should leave training to each branch manager
Training must be covered only in the BCP
bank.explanation: OM-5.5.15(d) lists the functions and controls the policy must address, including cyber training and awareness, along with asset, incident, vulnerability, configuration, access and third-party management.

bank.question: When drafting its cyber risk tolerance statement, which factors does OM-5.5.15(b) suggest the bank should consider?
options: Only the cost of security software
Only the number of IT staff
Customer impact, service downtime, negative publicity, regulatory penalties and financial loss
Only the share price
bank.explanation: OM-5.5.15(b) says the tolerance statement should be developed by considering impacts such as customer impact, service downtime, negative media publicity, regulatory penalties and financial loss.

bank.question: A compliance analyst cites the external attack surface management paragraph from the January 2024 CBB copy of Module OM as a rule in force since 2021. What is wrong with this?
options: Nothing, since every paragraph in the copy dates from 2021
The paragraph applies only to Volume 2 banks
The paragraph was deleted in 2022
That paragraph sits on a page marked 'XX 2024' and was a consultation proposal
bank.explanation: In the CBB-hosted copy issued with the 28 January 2024 consultation, OM-5.5.24A appears on a page marked 'XX 2024', showing it was proposed. Its final status must be checked in the current Rulebook.

bank.question: Senior management at Dilmun Coast Bank reports cyber incidents to the board only once a year. Which OM-5.5.10 duty does this fail?
options: Monthly reports to the CBB on every phishing email
Weekly reports to shareholders
Daily reports to customers
Quarterly or more frequent reports on all cyber incidents and their implications
bank.explanation: OM-5.5.10(f) requires senior management to prepare quarterly or more frequent reports on all cyber incidents, internal and external, and their implications for the bank.

bank.question: Criminals are sending emails that appear to come from Dilmun Coast Bank's domain. Which control set in OM-5.5.19 helps receiving servers reject such spoofed mail?
options: SPF, DKIM and DMARC on the bank's mail domain
A web application firewall
Privileged access management
Network access control on branch ports
bank.explanation: OM-5.5.19 requires anti-spoofing measures that authenticate the bank's mail server, such as SPF, DKIM and DMARC. The other controls protect web apps, admin accounts and network ports.

bank.question: Dilmun Coast Bank wants to use an e-signature service whose emails come from the service provider's own domain. What does OM-5.5.21A allow?
options: Any domain without approval if customers agree
No exceptions: only the bank's domain can ever be used
Additional domains subject to CBB approval, for example for third-party services arranged with customers
Any domain if the email contains no links
bank.explanation: OM-5.5.21A allows additional email domains, subject to CBB approval, in cases such as head or regional office emails and third-party services arranged in advance with customers, for example document management services.

bank.question: A product manager wants to send an SMS campaign to all customers with a shortened link to a new savings offer. Which two OM-5.5.21 rules does this break?
options: The link is unprompted by customer action, and it is shortened
It uses SMS instead of a letter, and it mentions a product
It is sent to all customers, and it is in English
It is a marketing message, and it is sent in the evening
bank.explanation: OM-5.5.21(a) limits links in SMS to messages resulting from a customer request or action, and (b) tells banks not to use shortened links in customer messages.

bank.question: Which list of safeguards does OM-5.5.21(c) give, of which a bank must use one or more when sending links to customers?
options: Clear instructions, a prior call, transaction details, or password or biometric authentication
Bright colours, larger text, an emoji or a QR code
A shortened link, a free email domain, or a pop-up
A discount code, a deadline, or a prize draw
bank.explanation: OM-5.5.21(c) lists clear instructions, prior notification such as a call, transaction details such as amount and merchant, and other verification such as password or biometric authentication.

bank.question: An employee clicks a link in a phishing email and enters her network password before realising. What should she do first?
options: Report it immediately to the SOC with details of what she entered
Change her password quietly and say nothing
Wait to see whether anything unusual happens
Forward the email to all colleagues as a warning
bank.explanation: Fast reporting lets the SOC reset credentials, contain any access and check whether the incident must be reported to the CBB. Hiding the mistake gives the attacker time.

bank.question: What did the CBB's January 2021 Benefitpay warning say about how Benefitpay requests personal information?
options: It requests personal information only through shortened links
It requests CPR updates by SMS once a year
It never requests personal information through SMS
It asks customers to reply to SMS with their PIN
bank.explanation: The CBB warned the public not to click the link in the fake SMS and stated that Benefitpay will never request personal information through SMS.

bank.question: Which OM-5.5.18 control limits the exploitation of both privileged and non-privileged accounts and monitors how they are used?
options: Identity and access management solutions
A secure web gateway
Data leakage prevention
Endpoint protection
bank.explanation: OM-5.5.18(k) requires identity and access management solutions to limit exploitation of, and monitor, privileged and non-privileged accounts. PAM under (e) focuses on privileged access to critical assets.

bank.question: OM-5.5.22 lists factors for periodic cyber threat assessments. Which factor relates directly to the risk that a member of staff misuses access?
options: Insider threats among cyber threat entities
Dark web surveillance only
Changes in regional threat severity
Attacks on other organisations
bank.explanation: OM-5.5.22(a) lists cyber threat entities including cyber criminals, cyber activists and insider threats. Insider risk is one reason awareness and access controls matter for every employee.

bank.question: A finance officer receives an email from a supplier asking to change bank details for the next payment. The email address is correct, but the supplier's mailbox may have been hacked. What is the safest control?
options: Accept it, because the address is genuine
Ask the sender to confirm by replying to the email
Confirm the change by calling the supplier on a number already held on file
Make half the payment to each account
bank.explanation: A hijacked mailbox sends from the genuine address, so the address alone proves nothing. Out-of-band verification through known contact details is the reliable control against payment-change fraud.

bank.question: Dilmun Coast Bank has used the same external penetration testing firm for three years. What does OM-5.5.28 require?
options: Nothing, as long as the firm is certified
Change the independent testers at least every two years
Stop external testing and use internal staff only
Ask the CBB to appoint a tester
bank.explanation: OM-5.5.28(d) requires tests by internal and external independent third parties, which should be changed at least every two years.

bank.question: A December penetration test finishes on 15 December. When is the report due to the CBB, and how long must it be kept?
options: By 31 December, and kept for one year
By 15 January, and kept for ten years
By 28 February, and kept for five years from the report date
By 31 March, and kept until the next test
bank.explanation: OM-5.5.61 requires the report within two months after the end of the testing month (its example: a December test by 28 February) and retention for five years from the report date, with the mitigation steps.

bank.question: Which feature distinguishes a red teaming exercise from a standard penetration test, as described in OM-5.5.29?
options: It is always done by the bank's own IT team
It tests detection and response quietly, rather than finding as many vulnerabilities as possible
It covers only the bank's website
It must be run every month
bank.explanation: OM-5.5.29 explains that a red team targets the organisation's detection and response, possibly across cyber, social and physical fronts, trying to reach sensitive information quietly, rather than listing all vulnerabilities.

bank.question: At 23:30 on a Friday the SOC confirms that a third-party provider's breach has exposed Dilmun Coast Bank customer data. Does OM-5.5.57 apply, and when?
options: No, because the breach happened at a third party
Yes, but only from the next business day
Yes: external incidents compromising customer data count, so the CBB must be called by 00:30
No, unless the data includes card numbers
bank.explanation: OM-5.5.57 covers any cyber incident, internal or external, that compromises customer information or disrupts critical services. The one-hour limit runs from occurrence or detection, including nights and weekends.

bank.question: The bank called the CBB within an hour and sent Section A on time. Ten days later, the root cause is still unknown. What should it do?
options: Delay Section B until the root cause is known
Submit Section B on time with as much information as possible, then keep sending weekly updates
Withdraw Section A and start again
Tell the CBB the incident is closed
bank.explanation: OM-5.5.58 sets the 10-calendar-day deadline and weekly updates until resolution, and OM-5.5.59 says to submit with as much information as possible even if not all details are known.

bank.question: Which item is listed in OM-5.5.60 as part of the comprehensive cyber incident report?
options: Who discovered the incident, such as a provider, customer or employee
The personal phone numbers of all board members
A list of every employee's training scores
The bank's quarterly profit forecast
bank.explanation: OM-5.5.60 lists discovery date and time, time to restore critical services, who discovered it, incident type, impact, affected systems and technical details, root cause and actions taken.

bank.question: The SOC detects ransomware spreading across branch PCs. Under OM-5.5.34, what may containment involve?
options: Paying the ransom immediately
Isolating or shutting down affected systems after weighing business impact
Deleting all logs to stop the spread
Waiting for the next penetration test
bank.explanation: OM-5.5.34 says that once an incident is detected, banks should activate containment, which may include shutting down or isolating affected systems after considering costs, business impact and operational risk.

bank.question: During an incident, the bank's Record Keeper is unsure what to log. What does OM-5.5.41 say the incident log should contain?
options: Only the final outcome once the incident is closed
Only technical data from the firewall
Only messages sent to the media
All notifications, decisions and actions, logged close to when they happen, with status and owner
bank.explanation: OM-5.5.41 asks for an incident log documenting all notifications, decisions and actions as close as possible to when they occur, including status and the person responsible, stored securely and in a legally admissible way.

bank.question: A cyber incident at Dilmun Coast Bank may affect other banks through a shared payment link. What does OM-5.5.43 suggest?
options: Keep the information internal to protect reputation
Post technical details publicly on social media
Wait for other banks to report first
Assess the wider impact and report it to the CBB if it may be systemic
bank.explanation: OM-5.5.43 says banks should assess effects on customers and the wider banking system and report the results to the CBB if the incident may have systemic impact. Non-sensitive data can also be shared through MISP.

bank.question: A police officer visits a Riffa branch and asks verbally for a customer's statements, without any written request or court order. The branch manager asks Maryam what to do. What is the best answer?
options: Hand them over, since the police can always see bank records
Give a summary of balances only
Do not hand them over; refer the request to compliance or legal to check the legal basis
Ask the customer's employer for permission
bank.explanation: Article 117 permits disclosure under a provision of law, a competent court order or a CBB instruction, among others. Whether a legal basis exists must be checked by compliance or legal; branch staff should not decide on a verbal request.

bank.question: Which statement about Article 118 of the CBB Law is accurate?
options: It allows any bank employee to disclose information to journalists
It sets out when the CBB itself may disclose confidential information it receives
It requires banks to publish customer lists
It abolishes banking confidentiality for corporate customers
bank.explanation: Article 118 lists when the Central Bank may disclose confidential information: in the Article 117 cases, for measures to protect the stability and trust of the system, and in cooperation with international or competent bodies.

bank.question: An employee emails a file of customer CPR numbers to her personal webmail to work from home. Which controls and rules are engaged?
options: Only the cyber insurance rules
Data leakage prevention under OM-5.5.18 and the CBB Law's confidentiality duty
Only the penetration testing rules
None, because she is a bank employee
bank.explanation: DLP under OM-5.5.18(b) aims to stop confidential data leaving the bank, and customer information is confidential under Articles 116-117. Sending it to personal email puts it outside the bank's protection.

bank.question: A customer gives verbal consent on a recorded call for the bank to share her loan details with a named mortgage broker. Later, a different broker asks for the same details. What should the bank do?
options: Share the details, as consent has been given once
Share them if the second broker works in the same building
Share only the loan amount
Refuse the second broker, since the customer's approval covered only the named broker
bank.explanation: Article 117 requires the unequivocal approval of the person the information relates to. Consent given for one named recipient does not extend to others.

bank.question: Which statement about Bahrain's PDPL is accurate at the level taught in this quest?
options: It is a CBB circular issued in 2024
It applies only to health data
It is Law No. 30 of 2018 and sets general duties for processing personal data
It removes the need for data classification at banks
bank.explanation: The Personal Data Protection Law is Law No. 30 of 2018, supervised by the Personal Data Protection Authority. It adds general data protection duties and does not replace Module OM controls.

bank.question: An email to a Dilmun Coast Bank manager appears to come from a foreign financial regulator, carries its logo and a signed letter, and asks for customer data to support 'compensation claims'. What does the CBB's 2019 CySEC warning suggest?
options: A regulator's logo proves the request is genuine
Logos and signatures can be faked; verify through compliance using known contact details
Foreign regulators may collect customer data from any bank employee
Reply with the data but mark it confidential
bank.explanation: The CBB's June 2019 warning described scammers copying CySEC's name, logo, stamp and signatures to seek fees and personal data. Requests from authorities must be verified and handled through compliance under Article 117.

bank.question: A colleague asks you to look up a famous customer's balance 'out of curiosity'. Why is this a problem even though no information leaves the bank?
options: Access should follow need to know under data classification, and customer information is confidential
It is not a problem if no one outside the bank finds out
It is only a problem if the customer complains
It is a problem only for corporate customers
bank.explanation: OM-5.5.12 links data classification to who has access and what use is appropriate, and Article 116 makes information on a customer's private affairs confidential. Curiosity is not a business need.

bank.question: Which pair of laws together shape how a Bahraini conventional bank must protect customer information, beyond the CBB Rulebook?
options: The Companies Law and the Labour Law
The Traffic Law and the Commercial Register Law
The Income Tax Law and the Customs Law
The CBB Law (Law No. 64 of 2006) and the Personal Data Protection Law (Law No. 30 of 2018)
bank.explanation: Articles 116-120 of the CBB Law set banking confidentiality, and the PDPL sets general personal data duties. Module OM then adds the technical and organisational controls.

bank.question: Dilmun Coast Bank delivers the same 20-minute cyber video to all staff each year and records 100% completion. Which OM-5.5 requirements may it still fail?
options: Penetration testing and red teaming
The single email domain rule
Cyber insurance and RTO setting
Role-specific training (OM-5.5.56), extra training for higher-risk staff and evaluating effectiveness (OM-5.5.54)
bank.explanation: Completion of a generic course does not provide regular role-specific training for executives, cyber, IT and high-risk staff, additional training for higher-risk staff, or evidence of improved awareness.

bank.question: After a phishing simulation, the CISO finds that the contact centre has a much higher click rate than other teams. What fits best with OM-5.5.55 and OM-5.5.56?
options: Discipline every agent who clicked and stop simulations
Hide the results to protect morale
Treat the team as higher-risk and give it extra, role-specific training, then re-measure
Exclude the team from future simulations
bank.explanation: OM-5.5.55 calls for additional training for higher-risk staff and OM-5.5.56(d) for role-specific training for high-risk staff the bank identifies. Re-measuring supports the effectiveness check in OM-5.5.54.

bank.question: Which obligation in OM-5.5.55 goes beyond formal courses?
options: Paying staff a bonus for completing training
Asking staff to buy their own antivirus
Keeping relevant employees informed of current cyber security breaches and threats
Requiring each employee to hold a CISSP
bank.explanation: OM-5.5.55 requires that all relevant employees be informed of current cyber breaches and threats, for example through threat bulletins, in addition to regular training.

bank.question: The board asks why it must attend cyber training when it already receives reports. What is the best answer under Module OM?
options: OM-5.5.56(a) requires regular role-specific training for the executive board and senior management
Board training is optional under Module OM
Only the CISO needs training, as the board delegates cyber
Board members are trained only if an incident occurs
bank.explanation: OM-5.5.56(a) lists the executive board and senior management among those who must receive regular role-specific cyber training. Reports under OM-5.5.4 do not replace it.

bank.question: Dilmun Coast Bank's executive team has never practised a cyber crisis. Which OM-5.5 duty addresses this most directly?
options: The policy review cycle (OM-5.5.15)
The single email domain (OM-5.5.21)
The data classification guidance (OM-5.5.12)
A programme of exercises such as attack simulations, war games and table-tops (OM-5.5.50)
bank.explanation: OM-5.5.50 requires a programme for exercising response mechanisms using simulations, war games and table-top exercises, involving technical staff, the crisis team, decision-makers and spokespersons.

bank.question: A critical payments system's recovery after a cyber attack took far longer than its defined RTO. Which OM-5.5 requirement was not met?
options: Penetration tests must be run twice a year (OM-5.5.28)
Critical systems must be able to recover within the defined RTO (OM-5.5.48)
Customer emails must use one domain (OM-5.5.21)
The board must discuss cyber (OM-5.5.1)
bank.explanation: OM-5.5.48 requires banks to ensure all critical systems can recover from a cyber breach within the bank's defined RTO, to provide important or minimum services.

bank.question: Which document must include a recovery plan for systems, operations and services after a cyber incident, under OM-5.5.52?
options: The annual report
The business continuity plan
The staff handbook
The marketing plan
bank.explanation: OM-5.5.52 requires the business continuity plan to be comprehensive and include recovery of systems, operations and services arising from a cyber security incident.

bank.question: During a CBB review, the examiner asks how the bank knows its cyber awareness programme works. Which evidence is strongest?
options: Trend data from simulations and incident reports showing better reporting and fewer clicks
A signed attendance sheet from last year's course
The training vendor's brochure
A statement from the CISO that staff are aware
bank.explanation: OM-5.5.54 asks the bank to evaluate improvement in awareness and preparedness. Measured trends in behaviour show effectiveness; attendance and assurances do not.
